html:
A city of the Indus Valley civilisation on Khadir island in the Rann of Kutch, in today's Gujarat, India. People lived there from about 2650 BCE to about 1450 BCE.

Kutch is dry, so the city's builders made water their main work. They cut a chain of large stone reservoirs into the rock, dammed two seasonal streams and led their flow into the tanks. Few ancient cities managed scarce rain so carefully.

The city had three parts: a walled citadel, a middle town and a lower town, all built of stone, unlike the brick of Mohenjo-daro. Near one gate lay ten large signs of the Indus script, perhaps once a signboard, the longest Indus inscription known.

Like Lothal, Dholavira sat on trade routes by sea and land, the network that reached Sumer. It declined as the wider civilisation broke up, perhaps hastened by the 4.2 kiloyear drought. It became a World Heritage Site in 2021.
sum: A city of the Indus Valley civilisation on Khadir island in the Rann of Kutch, in today's Gujarat, India. People lived there from about 2650 BCE to about 1450 BCE.
